To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The absorption of electromagnetic radiation by a metal can be anomalously high, even exceeding 100%, if the metal has a rough surface with a periodic profile and the wavelength of the pump radiation is commensurable with the period of the surface relief; (2) the absorption of radiation is anomalously high if the pump radiation has an intensity exceeding a certain threshold value, the value of which depends on the modulation depth of the surface relief and the period of the relief.
a rough surface of a condensed medium can absorb 100% of the incident light and that it is heated by the incident radiation faster than the corresponding flat surface.
the absorption of light by a metal surface can exceed 100% and that the rate of laser heating can be increased by several orders of magnitude by using a corrugated surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effect of a spatially periodic relief on the absorption of light and heating of a metal surface by laser radiation.
the study of the diffraction of electromagnetic waves by surfaces with a large modulation depth of the relief, and the development of a new method for the control of laser heating of condensed media.
the development of a new method of laser heating and with the study of the conditions for the anomalously fast heating.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a surface with a large amplitude of modulation of the profile can be a very efficient absorber for electromagnetic radiation.
the proposed theory provides an explanation for the observed anomalously high absorptiveness of a rough surface and for anomalously fast heating in a wide range of parameters of the problem.
the theory developed in the present paper is the first one to describe in a quantitative way the anomalous absorption of electromagnetic radiation in rough surfaces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a corrugated surface of condensed media is a promising object for the development of high-temperature lasers, high-power lasers, and high-temperature plasma sources.

we have developed a theory for the diffraction on a rough surface of a metal, which is applicable for large amplitudes of the surface relief, i.e., when the corrugation is of the same order of magnitude as the wavelength.
the proposed theory can predict the conditions for the appearance of the anomalies and can be used for their control.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a surface of a solid body can have anomalously high absorption of electromagnetic radiation when the amplitud of the modulation of its relief is large.
the diffraction of electromagnetic radiation by a rough surface can lead to the anomalously high absorption of energy in the surface layer and to the anomalously fast heating.
the surface profile of a metal surface can be used as a switch for the control of the absorption and heat generation rate of a metal surface.
